message.content:
Research question: What are the actual, current, official requirements/preconditions/gotchas for each native publish tool callisto shells out to (or might shell out to), that a spec for callisto's publish/distribution model needs to be grounded in?

Context: callisto is a Rust-based, polyglot (Cargo/npm/PyPI) release-engineering CLI at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto. It shells out to native tools to execute real publishes rather than reimplementing registry logic itself (confirmed: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs invokes `cargo publish`, `npm publish`/`pnpm publish`/`yarn npm publish`/`bun publish`, `python -m build` + `twine upload`). It has a `PublishTarget` enum (crates/callisto-model/src/ecosystem.rs) with CratesIo/Npm/Pypi/NuGet/GitHubRelease/None variants — NuGet and GitHubRelease currently warn-and-skip (not implemented). A prior research pass this session recommended, tentatively, adding real GitHub Release asset upload (via `gh release upload`) for prebuilt CLI binaries — this needs grounding in gh CLI's/GitHub Releases' actual documented requirements (e.g. does a release need to exist before assets can be uploaded to it? what does `gh release create` vs `gh release upload` actually require/support?).

The maintainer now wants deep, docs-grounded research (not general knowledge) across:
1. GitHub Releases / `gh` CLI (release creation, asset upload, requirements/preconditions)
2. npm publishing via pnpm specifically (pnpm publish conventions, npm registry requirements, provenance/2FA, workspace-aware publish)
3. cargo publishing (cargo publish requirements, --locked semantics, crates.io publishing guide, workspace publishing)
4. PyPI/twine (since callisto already publishes here) and NuGet (since it's a stubbed target) if time permits

Map sources for this research:
- Internal: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs` (the actual current publish invocations for each ecosystem — read the real flags/args used today, this is the baseline to compare official docs against), `crates/callisto-model/src/ecosystem.rs` (PublishTarget enum), `docs/06-publishing.md` (callisto's own publishing docs).
- External: official docs for `gh release create`/`gh release upload` (cli.github.com/manual or GitHub CLI docs), GitHub Releases API/concepts docs, npm CLI `npm publish` docs (docs.npmjs.com), pnpm `pnpm publish` docs (pnpm.io), Cargo Book's "Publishing on crates.io" chapter (doc.rust-lang.org/cargo), crates.io publishing requirements, PyPI/twine upload docs (packaging.python.org, twine.readthedocs.io), NuGet `dotnet nuget push`/publishing docs (learn.microsoft.com/nuget) if scope allows.

Scope: external (external sources are the whole point of this pass — the internal code is just the baseline to compare against, not the primary target).

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
